leads.summary: Open PR #9031's shell-owner check makes this PR's new menu-select fixture fail if both merge
leads.location: test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh:20-48; bin/omarchy-menu-select:110-112; related PR #9031 bin/omarchy-menu-select (merged copy merged-9031/bin/omarchy-menu-select:112-123)
leads.consequence: The fixture stubs omarchy-shell but never supplies a quickshell owner. #9031 calls menu_shell_pid before invoking that stub. In an isolated head plus #9031 merge, the first test exits 1 with 'omarchy-menu-select: no running Omarchy shell to show the menu'; the entire test file stops before testing --default-index, even though the production features are compatible. Adapt the fixture to model the new owner check (or inject a test seam) when reconciling the PRs. GitHub currently reports #9031 MERGEABLE against quattro, and the two heads are diverged, not stacked.
leads.triage: confirmed: coordinator source read of #9031 diff and PR test; Opus runtime follow-up (followup-9031.md). Published as new finding.

leads.summary: A missing --default-index value followed by another menu flag silently swallows that flag
leads.consequence: Passing 'Pick a b c -- --default-index --width 400' does not produce the documented 'requires a value' error. Instead --width is stored as the index and coerced to 0, 400 is ignored, the payload omits width, and the menu appears with the wrong initial row and default width. An omitted value at end is rejected, making this particular ordering surprising. Reject flag-looking values and unexpected post-'- -' tokens before sending the payload. This affects callers building an optional flag sequence as well as direct users.
leads.triage: dropped: same parsing convention as existing --width/--maxheight at base; only caller passes a number.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12135#issuecomment-5855802650), checked at head `0886701` on base `bf44355`.

**Outcome:** the force-push since the earlier review is a rebase. The 13 commits carry the same changes as the previously reviewed head `b9535ec`. `bin/omarchy-transcode`, `bin/omarchy-menu-select`, the two new test files and the notification card are byte-identical, and the PR's additions to `menu-test.sh` are unchanged. The earlier findings all still apply. One note is reframed below, and one new interaction with open PR #9031 is added.

**Verified** again at `0886701`:
- Explicit `medium` and a menu-picked `medium` give the same ffmpeg argv and byte-identical output as base on a synthetic clip.
- `--width 1e1000` still hangs on base and emits `0` at head.
- The three changed test files pass at head and fail against the base code.
- The full `test/shell` suite fails the same 11 files on base and head in this sandbox (pre-existing, not caused by this PR). The earlier review counted six in its environment.
- The branch merges cleanly onto the current `quattro` tip (`3faafba`), and the three PR tests pass on the merge result.

| Earlier finding | At `0886701` |
|---|---|
| Three-argument video command opens a quality menu | Still present, see the addition below |
| `(<1 MB).` completion body cut off by StyledText | Still present |
| `-2`, `-3` collision suffixes described as unchanged | Still present. The suffix loop now comes from commit `8c2e973`; `f523e4d` is no longer on the branch |
| `clip.mp4 avi` shows the resolution menu before rejecting the format | Still present |
| A 4th positional on a picture now fails | Reframed below |
| Sizes in MiB labelled "MB" | Still present |
| Manual promises a size estimate for every video quality row | Still present |
| Optional test improvement: `--default-index` caller sweep (`test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh:129-134`) | Still present |
| Planning references in shipped comments | Still present |
| Related open PRs (#6698, #11057, #11877, #12363, #13043, #7320, #7610, #7954, #11580) | Still apply. All nine are open, and the conflicts were rechecked against the current tip |

**Addition to the three-argument finding:** the PR description says omitting quality "reproduces today's encoder flags" and that the non-interactive callers (keybinding, Nautilus extension, menu action) "never pay for" ffprobe. Those three callers are interactive: they pass no format or resolution. The three-argument form was the non-interactive shape, and it now waits on `Select quality` (for mp4, after two ffprobe calls). Open PR #13360 already carries a commit ("Keep transcode clipboard tests compatible with quality prompts") that answers this menu in its own three-argument tests. The earlier suggested change still applies.

**Reframed: pictures with a 4th argument.** The PR description states that pictures "reject a 4th positional", so this is an intended change rather than an oversight. The earlier note stands as information only.

### Combined with open PR #9031, the new `menu-select-test.sh` fails

#9031 ("Stop menu commands waiting forever…") and this PR merge cleanly in either order. #9031 changes `bin/omarchy-menu-select` in two ways that matter here:
- It sources a new `omarchy-menu-handshake` helper by bare name, so the helper is looked up on `PATH`.
- It exits unless a `quickshell` process serving `$OMARCHY_PATH/shell` is running.

This PR's new `test/shell.d/menu-select-test.sh` runs the real `omarchy-menu-select` and stubs only `omarchy-shell`. On `quattro` plus both PRs:

| Setup for `menu-select-test.sh` | Result |
|---|---|
| As written, headless | fails at the first assertion: `omarchy-menu-handshake: No such file or directory` |
| `$ROOT/bin` on `PATH` | fails: `no running Omarchy shell to show the menu` |
| `OMARCHY_PATH=$ROOT`, `$ROOT/bin` on `PATH`, plus a stand-in process named `quickshell` whose command line contains `$ROOT/shell` | 12 ok |

`transcode-quality-test.sh` is unaffected because it stubs `omarchy-menu-select` entirely. The merged `menu-test.sh` passes. With a stubbed shell, ffmpeg and ffprobe, the combined production path still resolves the highlight to `medium` (`defaultIndex: 1`) and passes `-crf 23` to ffmpeg.

**Impact:** whichever of the two PRs lands second leaves `menu-select-test.sh` failing on headless runs and anywhere no matching Omarchy shell is running. `docs/testing.md` says tests must not depend on an installed Omarchy and must stay green on headless machines, so relying on a live shell is not an option.

**Suggested change:** in `menu-select-test.sh`, set `OMARCHY_PATH=$ROOT`, put `$ROOT/bin` on `PATH` and start a stand-in `quickshell` process whose command line contains `$ROOT/shell`, as in the passing row above. Alternatively, coordinate the test change with #9031's author so that it lands with whichever PR merges second.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source comparison of the old and new commit series and bases, plus source review of head `0886701` and open PR #9031 (head `aa732d0`). The PR tests, the full `test/shell` suite and behaviour probes ran in an isolated sandbox with real ffmpeg and ImageMagick on synthetic media. The menu, notification and clipboard were stubbed. StyledText truncation was measured offscreen with a bare Qt `Text`, not the notification card. The combined #9031 checks used a stand-in `quickshell` process, a stubbed shell and stubbed ffmpeg and ffprobe, not a real Quickshell. Conflicts come from merges of public branch heads as of 2026-09-28. No live desktop was used, and no real 4K encode was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
